section_summary.extract_value: This section explores the significant role of intelligence in creative achievement, attributing it to the link between intelligence and ideational originality, and the complex nature of creative tasks. It reviews several longitudinal studies that demonstrate intelligence's predictive power for creative achievement, including reanalyses of Torrance's data (Plucker, 1999; Cramond et al., 2005; Runco et al., 2010), a study on gifted 13-year-olds (Wai et al., 2005), and a 45-year longitudinal study (Feist and Barron, 2003). The discussion also touches upon the threshold hypothesis, noting that while some studies (Jauk et al., 2013; Karwowski & Gralewski, 2013) found partial support for it regarding creative potential, no such threshold was observed for creative achievement itself.
